There is already AppBundle which is a similar but different thing. 

We use the type2-runtime and if not we use the uruntime which is 100% compatible with the appimage runtime down to the CLI arguments.

Same tooling was used by Probono to make the [PrusaSlicer AppImage](https://github.com/prusa3d/PrusaSlicer/issues/13653) and I have personally done several similar PRs to other projects that make the AppImages fully be able to run on any linux system, like the Ghostty AppImage I linked in the PR you made. 

Not to mention that not all the AppImages here use sharun either, like deadbeef, which just makes the differences even less.

So no, we are not different from AppImage, and sharun itself got some inspiration from the deploy everything mode of go-appimage, which is used by both inkscape and gimp.

The issue is that Gearlever uses `p7zip` to extract the .desktop and icon from the AppImage instead of just running the appimage with `--appimage-extract` and `p7zip` doesn't support dwarfs, which is used by some appimages here like citron and torzu. 

Alternative run the appimage with `--appimage-extract` and get [appimagetool](https://github.com/AppImage/appimagetool/releases/tag/continuous) and run `./appimagetool-x86_64.AppImage -n /path/to/extracted/appimage` to get a squashfs appimage to use with gearlever.

However note by doing this the appimage will get bigger and it will also crash when you send the PC to sleep due to a bug in the type2-runtime, so maybe try our fork of [appimagetool](https://github.com/pkgforge-dev/appimagetool-uruntime/releases/tag/continuous) that uses the squashfs uruntime and it should work with gearlever? It will still be bigger but shouldn't crash on sleep. 

Or much better, use something like [AM](https://github.com/ivan-hc/AM) or [soar](https://github.com/pkgforge/soar) to get those appimages, you get updates automatically as well which with gearlever last time I saw you had to give it the url to the appimage manually.

`soar install citron`

Hi, I'm the developer of Gear Lever. 
Just for clarification, the current Appimage spec [https://docs.appimage.org/reference/architecture.html](https://docs.appimage.org/reference/architecture.html) states that the current filesystem in use should be squashfs.

Running `--appimage-extract` has two downsides:
- It doesn't work with older appimages, or any appimage built with an older version of appimagekit.
- there is no way, that I am aware of, to know if the extraction script is available, in advance
- running an old appimage with `--appimage-extract` may lead to the app actually executing, which is not what we want

Do you know how I can extract an appimage with a dwarfs filesystem without running `--appimage-extract`? Thank you

> Just for clarification, the current Appimage spec https://docs.appimage.org/reference/architecture.html states that the current filesystem in use should be squashfs.

It says that the type2 runtime is using squashfs, [which is true](https://github.com/AppImage/type2-runtime). 

The [draft spec](https://github.com/AppImage/AppImageSpec/blob/master/draft.md#type-2-image-format) instead states that a valid type2-runtime must be an ELF with an appended filesystem.  Which this complies with. 

>It doesn't work with older appimages, or any appimage built with an older version of appimagekit.

Those are [type1](https://github.com/AppImage/AppImageSpec/blob/master/draft.md#type-1-image-format), which are ISO 9660, they are very **very** old and have a different magic bytes.

>Do you know how I can extract an appimage with a dwarfs filesystem without running --appimage-extract? Thank you

The easy solution is to just check the magic bytes first. But if you want to do it externally, you will have to call a dwarfs binary, which is even able to find the offset on its own. 

AM doesn't actually bother to do the check of the magic bytes, because of the +2000 appimages it has in the database, only one uses the old type1 runtime and it is some abandoned video editor lol

> The easy solution is to just check the magic bytes first. But if you want to do it externally, you will have to call a dwarfs binary, which is even able to find the offset on its own.

There is even another issue related to `--appimage-extract`: older versions don't support partial extraction, like `*.desktop` or `*.png` for example, which means you have to extract the whole app, which is slow and uses a low of space. 
Anyway, thanks for the help, I'll try to improve Gear Lever.
Looks like `dwarfsextract` is just what I need, super easy to use. Thank you

I finally solved the mystery of the official RetroArch Appimage. It seems that the Appimage was influenced by the system environment variables set by the distribution's native Retroarch package. This is why it couldn't find the resources folder. Even though the native Retroarch package was uninstalled, I reinstalled it and ran `apt purge retroarch` to purge the entire installation, and the Appimage was able to start correctly from the resources folder copied to `~/.config/retroarch`.

The fact that the appimage relies on OS variables seems to be intended behavior from what the developer told me, in order to locate a retroarch folder already existing on the system. But in my case only the variables from the previous native retroarch installation were still present, which caused disruptions!

env variables are problematic because they get inherited by child processes, **there is no fix** other than reworking all of POSIX/Unix. 

I have this where I talk about [LD_LIBRARY_PATH](https://github.com/pkgforge-dev/Anylinux-AppImages/blob/main/HOW-TO-MAKE-THESE.md) being problematic for the same reason. 

Or this issue I had with [QT_PLUGIN_PATH](https://github.com/pkgforge-dev/Citron-AppImage/issues/3#issuecomment-2632700757)

[Or this other issue we had with gdk](https://github.com/pkgforge-dev/ghostty-appimage/issues/36#issuecomment-2669645302)...

Once `HOME` gets changed there is no way to roll it back unless you modify everything else to unset the variable and then set it back to what you want. 

The only other possible method to change the location of `~/` is to spin a namespace, but this has its own set of issues not to mention it wouldn't work on some distros due to namespaces being disabled.

So yeah I will closing this because it is impossible to fix, if you have more questions check the pkgforge discord which the link is in the organization front page.

sharun is able to set env variables in its own without depending on the host shell. You can actually for example take Cromite and unset `PATH` and see that it still works: 

![Image](https://github.com/user-attachments/assets/6cfdf382-bc34-4491-9476-28698ed6104c)

Of course a few AppImages here (like GIMP) still need a dedicated `AppRun` script that depends on the host shell to work around some issues.

Also `sh` is mandated by POSIX and I don't really see why we should add it, even non FHS distros like NixOS make sure to have it available.

`bash` makes sense but it is rare for applications to call bash directly unless you application happens to be a script, the only time I saw that was with goverlay which I changed for sh.


What I don't see useful is bundling `xdg-open`, I mean we can do it but if you run into a system that doesn't have `xdg-open` then whatever `xdg-open` was going to launch originally is likely not there either 😆

Yeah, this of mine is just nitpicking, to make it (almost) fully independent from the host.
This would also assure that AnyLinux-AppImage versions of sh/bash & xdg-open are tested to not have any regressions compared to host's version which can potentially have.

It's the best AppImage building process so far imo.

> Yeah, this of mine is just nitpicking, to make it (almost) fully independent from the host. This would also assure that AnyLinux-AppImage versions of sh/bash & xdg-open are tested to not have any regressions compared to host's version which can potentially have.
> 
> It's the best AppImage building process so far imo.

I don't think anything we have here depends on `bash`. 

`sh` yes some appimages here depend on the host `sh`, but man this is a vital part of any unix system, if you have `sh` with a regression **you ran into some really really weird bug**, like I'm surprised the computer that has that issue even boots. 

Like I have never in my life see a regression in `sh`, I have seen a lot of people having issues with bashisms, but never that `sh` itself was broken 👀

Another issue is that we can't really bundle our own `sh`, because we are running into a limitation of the kernel: 

When you run say `xdg-open`, that script contains a shebang `#!/bin/sh`, this resolution **is done by the kernel itself to tell `/bin/sh` to run that file**

We can't have a relative interpreter like `#!$ORIGIN/bin/sh` because the kernel doesn't resolve `$ORIGIN`.  It would try to find a literal `$ORIGIN` dir in the current working dir. 

We could have a relative interpreter to the current working dir, but that would mean changing the current working dir to the random mountpoint of the appimage, **this is not ideal**, for example gimp shows the current working dir in the menu to open files, then all of the sudden you will see some random dir with a long name in the menu. 

Same with terminal emulators, they open at the current working dir, all of the sudden you terminal would be opening at some random path in `/tmp`. 

Of course there is another way, which is using `env` and have all the scripts/programs try `#!/usr/bin/env sh`, in that case then our bundled `sh` will be used, but I think you already saw the problem, we are depending on `/usr/bin/env` now 👀 Which on some old systems is actually not located there.

While technically possible, it is a lot of work because of the following issues: 

* Steam depends on python, it is not easy to make AppImages of python apps without containers, often times when you see an AppImage of a python app is because pyinstaller was used, which is able to turn python scripts to ELFs that can then be turned into AppImage, [Not to mention this breaks with the slightness version change of python](https://github.com/pkgforge-dev/puddletag-AppImage/pull/11)

* Steam also depends on 32bit libs, and Steam itself is not an ELF but a shell script, so getting all the needed deps is also going to be a lot of pain.

* Another issue is that Steam itself actually installs in the users home and then tries to use the dependencies of the host, meaning you will likely still need namespaces somewhere.

You have a `usr/share` dir in the AppImage, but `sharun` instead makes a top level `share` dir.

Just copy the contents of `usr/share` to `share` **and remove `XDG_DATA_DIRS` from the `AppRun`**, sharun already sets the variable on its own. That's all that's needed to fix that issue.

![Image](https://github.com/user-attachments/assets/27bc918f-018c-415b-b972-cb3b215060ca)

 
Some other suggestions/questions:

* I would also avoid making an `AppRun` script and instead make sharun the `AppRun` directly. But if you want the `AppRun` script instead use `#!/bin/sh` as the sheabang and that way it is POSIX, which yeah there are some linux systems that don't have bash by default 👀

* There is no need to be setting `LD_LIBRARY_PATH`, the thing is just nightmares. **And in fact the missing symbol errors you see in the screenshot above are because of that.**

What's the difference between pinning to a specific commit vs just leaving it to a specific version?

> What's the difference between pinning to a specific commit vs just leaving it to a specific version?

Difference is that pinning to the specific commit guarantees that you are pulling the code from that OG release version, while pinning to the release, only guarantees you that you are pulling the code from the release itself, which can be maliciously tampered if hostile takeover to the repo happens.
So it makes it safe from that scenario.

Fixed the XDG variable handling as requested. Now the library:

1. **Tracks parent environment properly** - Distinguishes between "parent had XDG_CONFIG_HOME/XDG_DATA_HOME set to X" vs "parent didn't have them set at all"

2. **Unsets portable variants when parent didn't have them** - If parent didn't have XDG_CONFIG_HOME/XDG_DATA_HOME set, the library unsets AppImage portable variants (ending in .config/.share) so applications use their defaults (~/.config and ~/.local/share)

3. **Restores only when parent had them set** - If parent had these variables set to specific values, restores to those original values

Added `is_portable_appimage_in_use()` function that checks all three variables (HOME, XDG_CONFIG_HOME, XDG_DATA_HOME) for their respective portable suffixes. rm -rf ./AppDir/share/glvnd ./AppDir/lib/dri ./AppDir/lib/gbm ./AppDir/lib/vdpau

./AppDir/sharun -g
./AppDir/AppRun

@Shikakiben here is a full explanation: 

* Desktop environments need to know what icon belongs to a running application. 

* To do this need just check the windows class (x11) or app id (wayland) of the running application.

* What they need to look for is found in the desktop entry, it is known as `StartupWMClass`. 

* Important `StartupWMClass` **does not set the info, it tells the desktop environment what the info is.**

* The problem here is that on GTK4 apps, GNOME in their infinite wisdom decided to class the app id different from the window class. So if you happen to set `StartupWMClass` to the value that is valid for `x11` **it breaks in wayland and viceversa.**

---

The only way we can solve this issue is by forcing the window class/app id to the same value in x11 and wayland, this will involve preloading a library to our appimages, haven't gotten around finishing that.

## Automated Dependency Updates

[Mend Renovate](https://www.mend.io/renovate/) keeps source code dependencies up-to-date using automated Pull Requests. It will scan repositories for package manager files (e.g. from npm/Yarn, Bundler, Composer, Go Modules, Pip/Pipenv/Poetry, Maven/Gradle, Dockerfile/k8s, and many more), and submit Pull Requests with updated versions whenever they are found.

This app is free to install for both public and private repositories. Service is provided complimentary of Mend (formerly known as WhiteSource) and no paid plan is required.

### Intelligent, helpful onboarding

![Onboarding](https://docs.renovatebot.com/assets/images/onboarding.png)

Install Mend Renovate risk-free and you'll first receive an onboarding Pull Request in each repository. It analyzes the repository files and describes what will happen next, so there's no surprises. 

### Unopinionated, highly flexible configuration

```json
{
  "rangeStrategy": "pin",
  "ignorePaths": ["examples/**"],
  "packageRules": [{
    "packagePatterns": ["^angular.*"],
    "groupName": "angular",
    "automerge": true
  }]
}
```

Modify any of Renovate's smart defaults with custom overrides at the repository, package file, dependency type, and package levels. 

### Support for monorepo directory structures

Renovate will scan all files in each repository to look for relevant package files. It will also group upgrades from the same monorepo into a single PR to ensure tests pass and PR noise is reduced. Natively supports Lerna and Yarn Workspaces with zero configuration necessary.

It is also works fine with a mix of package managers / languages within the same repository.

### Automatic lock file and checksum support

Renovate will generate updated lock files such as `package-lock.json` or `yarn.lock` if you're already using them. It will also automatically resolve any conflicts after merges.

### Ease the noise with custom schedules

```json
{
  "timezone": "America/New_York",
  "schedule": "before 5am every weekday",
  "lockFileMaintenance": {
    "enabled": true,
    "schedule": "after 10pm on sunday"
  },
  "packageRules": [{
    "packageNames": ["aws-sdk"],
    "schedule": "before 5am every wednesday"
  }]
}
```

Throttle updates however you want with schedules, configurable right down to the per-package level.

### Rules-based automerging

![automerging](https://docs.renovatebot.com/assets/images/automerged-pr.png)

Merge some updates without human intervention if they pass tests and satisfy your automerge rules.

## Automated Dependency Updates

[Mend Renovate](https://www.mend.io/renovate/) keeps source code dependencies up-to-date using automated Pull Requests. It will scan repositories for package manager files (e.g. from npm/Yarn, Bundler, Composer, Go Modules, Pip/Pipenv/Poetry, Maven/Gradle, Dockerfile/k8s, and many more), and submit Pull Requests with updated versions whenever they are found.

This app is free to install for both public and private repositories. Service is provided complimentary of Mend (formerly known as WhiteSource) and no paid plan is required.

### Intelligent, helpful onboarding

![Onboarding](https://docs.renovatebot.com/assets/images/onboarding.png)

Install Mend Renovate risk-free and you'll first receive an onboarding Pull Request in each repository. It analyzes the repository files and describes what will happen next, so there's no surprises. 

### Unopinionated, highly flexible configuration

```json
{
  "rangeStrategy": "pin",
  "ignorePaths": ["examples/**"],
  "packageRules": [{
    "packagePatterns": ["^angular.*"],
    "groupName": "angular",
    "automerge": true
  }]
}
```

Modify any of Renovate's smart defaults with custom overrides at the repository, package file, dependency type, and package levels. 

### Support for monorepo directory structures

Renovate will scan all files in each repository to look for relevant package files. It will also group upgrades from the same monorepo into a single PR to ensure tests pass and PR noise is reduced. Natively supports Lerna and Yarn Workspaces with zero configuration necessary.

It is also works fine with a mix of package managers / languages within the same repository.

### Automatic lock file and checksum support

Renovate will generate updated lock files such as `package-lock.json` or `yarn.lock` if you're already using them. It will also automatically resolve any conflicts after merges.

### Ease the noise with custom schedules

```json
{
  "timezone": "America/New_York",
  "schedule": "before 5am every weekday",
  "lockFileMaintenance": {
    "enabled": true,
    "schedule": "after 10pm on sunday"
  },
  "packageRules": [{
    "packageNames": ["aws-sdk"],
    "schedule": "before 5am every wednesday"
  }]
}
```

Throttle updates however you want with schedules, configurable right down to the per-package level.

### Rules-based automerging

![automerging](https://docs.renovatebot.com/assets/images/automerged-pr.png)

Merge some updates without human intervention if they pass tests and satisfy your automerge rules.

Not sure what the issue is, it will only attempt to guess the update information if `GITHUB_REPOSITORY` is set. 

`UPINFO` is a string that gets embedded in the appimage runtime, nothing bad happens if the info is wrong, just that [updating with appimageupdate](https://github.com/AppImageCommunity/AppImageUpdate) will not work.

electron apps can also have that structure. See [signal](https://github.com/pkgforge-dev/Signal-AppImage-Enhanced/blob/main/make-appimage.sh) In these cases you want to have the `AppDir` ready: ``` mkdir -p ./AppDir/bin cp -v ./program ./AppDir/bin cp -rv ./rest ./AppDir/bin quick-sharun ./AppDir/bin/* ```

> Not sure what the issue is, it will only attempt to guess the update information if `GITHUB_REPOSITORY` is set.

The problem is that gitea and GITHUB_REPOSITORY are there solely for backward compatibility, and gh-releases-zsync, which relies on the GitHub API, won't work with gitea. Essentially, it's a broken upinfo, but if it doesn't affect anything, then it's fine.

In that you should still try to fix that issue.

Updates with appimageupdate provide delta updates, [that is only the diff is downloaded](https://github.com/pkgforge-dev/AppImageUpdate-Enhanced-Edition?tab=readme-ov-file#appimageupdate-enhanced-edition-)

When not hosted on github `UPINFO` instead needs to contain an url, [see librewolf for example.](https://gitlab.com/librewolf-community/browser/appimage/-/blob/master/build_appimage.sh#L83)

There is a lot of apps that place files in `PWD`, that is a annoying and a problem. 

In those cases you might wanna consider making a hook that does the following: 

make a file in `AppDir/bin` with this name for example: `change-working-dir.src.hook`

```
dir=${XDG_CONFIG_HOME:-~/.config}/APPNAME-appimage
mkdir -p "$dir"
cd "$dir"
```

This way the app will make its own config directory and place those files in there since it will switch the working dir there always. 

Note that this introduces a problem if the application expects to be given relative files, for example this will break: 

```
./ranmdonapp.AppImage ./path/to/file/to/open
```

So it cannot be always use, anyways this is a problem with the app and not something you have to fix yourself.

Hi! I responded at the PR but here it goes again:

The main problem this causes (besides that it brings a lot of dependencies) is that installing SDL3 now pulls libpipewire, but that does not pull `pipewire-audio` which bypasses checks we have to make sure SDL3 does not attempt to use pipewire when we deploy it without it. 

See also https://github.com/libsdl-org/SDL/issues/14887 which the SDL folks fixed in 24 hours. 

This is not a problem for distributions, because distributions will not add incompatible packages that SDL will then dlopen, it is a problem for people that distribute binaries that link to SDL. SDL offers a lot of env variables to control which libraries it will use, all of that goes away when the mandatory linking is in place.

Correction: It is actually a bit of a problem for distributions as well, for example some AUR packages may now cause SDL to fail to launch if they change the dependencies that SDL now links directly against.

Before that SDL has fail safes in place that if it fails to dlopen XYZ library it will continue working, now this will cause it to stop working all together.

This does not work on alpine due to two issues. 

* `7z` is needed to extract some files that are downloaded. 

* it executes an `rvgl` script in the users home that depends on `bash`. **The script uses `#!/bin/bash` instead of `#!/usr/bin/env bash` which is a big problem for us here.**

---

Make sure to bundle `7z`, and in the base of `bash`, since the game itself hardcodes `/bin/bash` all we can do here is an exception and add a hook that checks for the precense of `/bin/bash` and if it is not present we send an error like this: 

```sh
if [ ! -x /bin/bash ]; then
    notify -de "ERROR: This game requires /bin/bash which is not present in this system!"
    exit 1
fi
```

Ideally upstream should update their scripts to use `#!/bin/sh` or `#!/usr/bin/env bash`. 

---

Note that on archlinux the `7z` binaries are some shell scripts, the real binaries are in some directories in `/usr/lib` btw

## Automated Dependency Updates

[Mend Renovate](https://www.mend.io/renovate/) keeps source code dependencies up-to-date using automated Pull Requests. It will scan repositories for package manager files (e.g. from npm/Yarn, Bundler, Composer, Go Modules, Pip/Pipenv/Poetry, Maven/Gradle, Dockerfile/k8s, and many more), and submit Pull Requests with updated versions whenever they are found.

This app is free to install for both public and private repositories. Service is provided complimentary of Mend (formerly known as WhiteSource) and no paid plan is required.

### Intelligent, helpful onboarding

![Onboarding](https://docs.renovatebot.com/assets/images/onboarding.png)

Install Mend Renovate risk-free and you'll first receive an onboarding Pull Request in each repository. It analyzes the repository files and describes what will happen next, so there's no surprises. 

### Unopinionated, highly flexible configuration

```json
{
  "rangeStrategy": "pin",
  "ignorePaths": ["examples/**"],
  "packageRules": [{
    "packagePatterns": ["^angular.*"],
    "groupName": "angular",
    "automerge": true
  }]
}
```

Modify any of Renovate's smart defaults with custom overrides at the repository, package file, dependency type, and package levels. 

### Support for monorepo directory structures

Renovate will scan all files in each repository to look for relevant package files. It will also group upgrades from the same monorepo into a single PR to ensure tests pass and PR noise is reduced. Natively supports Lerna and Yarn Workspaces with zero configuration necessary.

It is also works fine with a mix of package managers / languages within the same repository.

### Automatic lock file and checksum support

Renovate will generate updated lock files such as `package-lock.json` or `yarn.lock` if you're already using them. It will also automatically resolve any conflicts after merges.

### Ease the noise with custom schedules

```json
{
  "timezone": "America/New_York",
  "schedule": "before 5am every weekday",
  "lockFileMaintenance": {
    "enabled": true,
    "schedule": "after 10pm on sunday"
  },
  "packageRules": [{
    "packageNames": ["aws-sdk"],
    "schedule": "before 5am every wednesday"
  }]
}
```

Throttle updates however you want with schedules, configurable right down to the per-package level.

### Rules-based automerging

![automerging](https://docs.renovatebot.com/assets/images/automerged-pr.png)

Merge some updates without human intervention if they pass tests and satisfy your automerge rules.
